Understanding #kubernetes pod lifecycle phases for effective #troubleshooting 🧐☸

✅ Pods follow a defined lifecycle, starting in the 'Pending' phase, moving through 'Running' if at least one of its primary containers starts OK, and then through either the 'Succeeded' or 'Failed' phases depending on whether any container in the Pod terminated in failure

✅ The phase of a #Pod is a simple, high-level summary of where the pod is in its lifecycle and it's part of "PodStatus" object that defines number of phases:
▶ 𝐏𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠: Pod has been accepted by the #k8s cluster, but one or more of the #containers has not been set up and made ready to run. This includes time a Pod spends waiting to be scheduled as well as the time spent downloading container images over the network
▶ 𝐑𝐮𝐧𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠:  Pod has been bound to a node, and all of the containers have been created. At least one container is still running, or is in the process of starting or restarting
▶ 𝐒𝐮𝐜𝐜𝐞𝐞𝐝𝐞𝐝: All containers in the Pod have terminated in success, and will not be restarted
▶ 𝐅𝐚𝐢𝐥𝐞𝐝: All containers in the Pod have terminated, and at least one container has terminated in failure. That is, the container either exited with non-zero status or was terminated by the system.
▶ 𝐔𝐧𝐤𝐧𝐨𝐰𝐧: the state of the Pod could not be obtained and it occurs due to an error in communicating with the node where the Pod should be running.

To track the phases between pod communication, "container lifecycle hooks" can be used to trigger events to run at certain points in a container's lifecycle !!

author: Carl Collins Chwabo
post_text:
DevSecOps: Building security into every stage of software delivery.

Security can no longer be a final checkpoint before production. Waiting until the end of development leads to costly fixes, delayed releases, and avoidable vulnerabilities.

That is where DevSecOps comes in.
DevSecOps brings together Development, Security, and Operations teams to make security a shared responsibility across the software development lifecycle. The goal: deliver applications quickly while ensuring security controls are integrated, automated, and continuously improved.

Instead of asking “Has this been secured?” only before deployment, DevSecOps asks security-focused questions at every stage:

• Planning: What are the security requirements and risks?

• Development: Are developers following secure coding practices?

• Code review: Are secrets or vulnerable dependencies being introduced?

• CI/CD: Has the application passed automated security tests?

• Deployment: Is the cloud or container configuration secure?

• Production: Are logs monitored and vulnerabilities remediated quickly?
Key DevSecOps tools

• CI/CD: Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD

• SAST: SonarQube, Semgrep, Checkmarx

• SCA: Snyk, Dependabot, OWASP Dependency-Check

• Secrets detection: GitGuardian, Gitleaks

• DAST: OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite

• Container security: Trivy, Docker Scout

• IaC security: Checkov, tfsec

• Cloud security: Wiz, Microsoft Defender
for Cloud, AWS Security Hub

• Runtime monitoring: Splunk, Elastic Security, Wazuh, Falco

How to implement DevSecOps

1. Build a shared security culture across Dev, Sec, and Ops.

2. Define secure coding standards and threat-modeling practices.

3. Integrate automated security checks into CI/CD pipelines.

4. Apply risk-based security gates (block only on critical issues).

5. Secure cloud and container environments with least privilege and continuous scanning.

6. Monitor continuously in production and integrate incident response.

7. Measure improvement: time to remediate, vulnerabilities caught pre-prod, test coverage.

DevSecOps is about reducing risk without sacrificing innovation. When security is automated early and continuously, organizations can deliver faster, respond better, and build greater trust in their digital services.

For cybersecurity teams, developers, and IT leaders, the question is no longer whether security should be part of DevOps. The real question is: how early, how consistently, and how effectively are we integrating it?

author: Rust Jobs 🦀
post_text:
Rust Hiring Report – Q3 2026

Full report in the comments 👇

Over the past few years, we've worked closely with companies hiring Rust engineers and with developers looking for Rust roles. Both sides raise the same problem: there is little clear information about this market. This covers not just compensation, but where the jobs are, which industries are hiring, and how much of the work is remote.

A few months ago, we built a crawler (written in Rust) and an AI extraction pipeline. They find companies hiring Rust developers and evaluate their openings. Many job descriptions list several languages, such as "5+ years of experience in a backend language like Java, C++, Rust or Go". So a search for "Rust" can't tell you if the role actually uses Rust. Instead, we labelled a few hundred job descriptions by hand. Then we tuned an AI prompt until it got good at spotting real Rust positions.

Here are a few interesting points from the report:

- 753 open Rust job ads at 305 companies as of 16 Sep 2026.
- 2,898 ads mention Rust somewhere, but only 753 (26%) actually require it.
- 165 of the 305 companies have exactly one open Rust ad.
- Around 80% of ads want a senior or staff-level developer.
- US median advertised base: $205k for senior, $228.5k for staff/principal (base only, no equity or bonus).
- US pay data comes almost entirely from a few states with pay transparency laws. Elsewhere, disclosure is rare: only 25 of 165 European ads showed a range.
- Rust ads stay open slightly longer: 68% were still posted 45 days after they appeared, vs 56% for the average ad on the same boards over the same period.
- Defense/aerospace/space is the biggest sector by role count (22.7% of ads), but crypto/web3 has more companies hiring.
- Remote: 35% of ads that state a work setup are fully remote. Defense is the exception, at under 10%.
- Top employers by volume: Anduril (50 ads), Cloudflare (23), K2 Space (18), NVIDIA (13).

Limitations:

- We only count companies with a public, crawlable careers page. Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Apple and Meta are absent from every figure because we can't crawl their career sites, not because they don't hire for Rust.

- Salary data is rare outside the few US states that require employers to advertise it.

If you have ideas to improve the report or you spot errors, please let us know!

Following up on my end-of-year #dataengineering predictions (https://lnkd.in/eD-dR8TJ), let's take a moment to reflect on the trends we saw in 2022 and what's brewing for 2023.

In #2022, we've seen a paradigm shift towards a declarative approach, shaping everything from infrastructure to orchestration and integration. The same principle lies at the heart of the flourishing semantic layer, promising an exciting, declarative future for metrics. ✨

Meanwhile, Rust is poised to revolutionize performance-heavy data applications, likely becoming the new Spark of the data world. For those navigating the small data seas, vector databases like DuckDB are becoming the go-to option, with an eye to support the AI wave on the horizon. Let's not forget - it's always about the data, not the other way around.

We've also noticed an upswing in metadata trends, with a focus on data cataloging, lineage, and discovery. And with GDPR and CCPA making waves, privacy and governance are becoming non-negotiables for every company, big or small.

Now, let's take a look at #2023. As we reveal the modern data stack (MDS), data modeling is making a comeback, offering a sense of order in the inevitable data chaos. But hold on, there's a caveat - many enterprises are grappling with how to harness the power of MDS. ️

This year is also witnessing the 'bundling' of MDS. Startups are consolidating (Transform into dbt), undergoing layoffs, and converging - evolution is the name of the game.

AI and generative AI, like our friend ChatGPT 🤖, are buzzing around, looking for ways to better integrate with data. While still more of a hype, many are keenly exploring these technologies' potential, and I can't wait to see how this story unfolds.

✅ Here are the "Recommended Labels" which should be applied to every resource object:

1️⃣ 𝐚𝐩𝐩.𝐤𝐮𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐭𝐞𝐬.𝐢𝐨/𝐧𝐚𝐦𝐞
👉 The name of the application
👉 Example: “mysql”

2️⃣ 𝐚𝐩𝐩.𝐤𝐮𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐭𝐞𝐬.𝐢𝐨/𝐢𝐧𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞
👉 A unique name identifying the instance of an application. To assign a non-unique name, use "app.kubernetes.io/name"
👉 For example, WordPress has a "app.kubernetes.io/name" of "mysql" while it has an instance name, represented as "app.kubernetes.io/instance" with a value of "mysql-abcxzy".
👉 Every instance of an application must have a unique name.

3️⃣ 𝐚𝐩𝐩.𝐤𝐮𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐭𝐞𝐬.𝐢𝐨/𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧
👉 The current version of the application.
👉 Example: "5.7.21"
👉 Common forms of values include:
🔸 semantic version
🔸 the Git revision hash for the source code.

4️⃣ 𝐚𝐩𝐩.𝐤𝐮𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐭𝐞𝐬.𝐢𝐨/𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐨𝐧𝐞𝐧𝐭
👉 The component within the architecture.
👉 Example: “database”

5️⃣ 𝐚𝐩𝐩.𝐤𝐮𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐭𝐞𝐬.𝐢𝐨/𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐭-𝐨𝐟
👉 The name of a higher-level application this one is part of.
👉 Example: “wordpress”

6️⃣ 𝐚𝐩𝐩.𝐤𝐮𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐭𝐞𝐬.𝐢𝐨/𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐝-𝐛𝐲

👉 Example: “helm”

🐘 Her Şey İçin Ayrı Bir Teknoloji Şart mı? PostgreSQL ile Mimariyi Sadeleştirmek
Projeye başlarken hemen "Buraya bir Elasticsearch basalım", "Hemen bir Redis kuralım" demek çok cazip gelir. Ancak genç yazılımcıların en sık sorduğu sorulardan biri şudur: PostgreSQL tek başına bu ekosistemde nelere kadirdir, hangi durumlarda harici araçlara gerek kalmaz?
PostgreSQL'i doğru kullanarak hangi senaryolarda harici araçlar yerine sadece onu tercih edebileceğinizi 7 maddede derledim:
1. Full-Text Search (Arama Motoru Yerine)
Alternatif: Elasticsearch / Meilisearch
PostgreSQL Çözümü: pg_trgm ve tsvector özellikleri sayesinde, küçük ve orta ölçekli uygulamalarda harici bir arama motoru kurma maliyetine girmeden gelişmiş metin arama ve benzerlik sorguları yapabilirsiniz.
2. Şemasız Veriler (NoSQL / MongoDB Yerine)
Alternatif: MongoDB
PostgreSQL Çözümü: Güçlü JSONB veri tipi ve GIN indeksleri sayesinde, ilişkisel verilerle esnek JSON verilerini aynı masada harmanlayabilir; NoSQL esnekliğini SQL güvencesiyle birleştirebilirsiniz.
3. Hafifletilmiş İş Kuyrukları (Job Queue / RabbitMQ Yerine)
Alternatif: RabbitMQ / Kafka
PostgreSQL Çözümü: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED mekanizması ile kuyruk tabloları oluşturarak, ekstra bir message broker kurmadan güvenli ve transaksiyonel arka plan görev kuyrukları yönetebilirsiniz.
4. Zaman Serisi Verileri (Time-Series Yerine)
Alternatif: InfluxDB / Timescale (Harici)
PostgreSQL Çözümü: Açık kaynaklı TimescaleDB eklentisini ekleyerek, metrikleri, IoT verilerini ve zaman serisi analizlerini doğrudan PostgreSQL üzerinde yüksek performansla saklayabilirsiniz.
5. Operasyonel Sadırlık ve Tek Kaynak (Single Source of Truth)
Avantajı: Genç ekipler için birden fazla farklı veritabanını (Cache, Search, NoSQL, SQL) yönetmek, yedeklemek ve monitor etmek büyük bir operasyonel yükdür. PostgreSQL ile bu karmaşıklığı minimuma indirebilirsiniz.
6. Ne Zaman Sınır Aşılır? (Doğru Yeri Bilmek)
Sınır: Saniyede yüz binlerce cache okuması (Redis seviyesi) veya milyarlarca logun anlık aranması (Elasticsearch seviyesi) gerektiğinde PostgreSQL zorlanabilir. İhtiyacın boyutunu iyi analiz etmek gerekir.
7. Öğrenme Eğrisi ve Temelleri Sağlam Tutmak

post_text:
"Tablodan 10 milyon satır sildik ama veritabanı boyutu bir milimetre bile inmedi..." 🗄️👻
​PostgreSQL kullanan ekiplerin yaşadığı en sinsi performans krizlerinden biri: Disk dolmak üzeredir, eski kayıtları DELETE edersiniz; ancak disk kullanımı düşmediği gibi sorgular daha da yavaşlar.
​Sebebi PostgreSQL'in çok sürümlü eşzamanlılık kontrolü (MVCC) mimarisidir.
​PostgreSQL'de bir satırı sildiğinizde veya güncellediğinizde (UPDATE işlemi aslında bir DELETE + INSERTtir), kayıt diskten anında silinmez; sadece "ölü" işaretlenir: Dead Tuple.
​Bu ölü satırlar zamanında temizlenmezse:
​Tablo ve indeksler hayalet verilerle şişer (Table & Index Bloat),
​RAM ve disk I/O'su boş sayfaları taramakla tükenir,
​İndeks ağaçları gereksiz genişlediği için arama süreleri katlanır.
​PostgreSQL'i bu hayalet yükten kurtarmak için uyguladığım 3 kritik adım:
​🧹 Bloat ve Autovacuum Yönetiminde 3 Kural
​1️⃣ Varsayılan Autovacuum'a Güvenmemek:
PostgreSQL'in varsayılan autovacuum eşikleri büyük tablolarda çok geç devreye girer. Yoğun yazma alan tablolarda eşiği önden çekmek gerekir:
ALTER TABLE orders SET (autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor = 0.05);
Böylece ölü satır oranı %5'e ulaştığı an temizlik başlar.
​2️⃣ İndeksleri Kilitlemeden Yenilemek (REINDEX CONCURRENTLY):
Veri silinse bile B-Tree indeks sayfaları işletim sistemine geri verilmez; indeks parçalanmış kalır. Canlı akışı ve yazmaları kesmeden indeksleri sıkılaştırmak için:
REINDEX TABLE CONCURRENTLY orders;
Bu komut çoğu zaman indeks boyutunu %60-70 küçültür ve belleği rahatlatır.
​3️⃣ Açık Kalan Transaction'ları (Idle in Transaction) Avlamak:
Arka planda unutulan tek bir açık transaction, kendisinden sonraki hiçbir ölü satırın VACUUM edilmesine izin vermez. idle_in_transaction_session_timeout ile bu asılı oturumları otomatik düşürmek şarttır.
​💼 Sizin de PostgreSQL altyapınızda şişen disk boyutları, anlamsızca yavaşlayan sorgular veya Autovacuum optimizasyonu ihtiyaçlarınız var mı?

post_text:
The Story of PyTorch :
PyTorch, a leading deep learning framework, was created by Facebook's AI Research (FAIR) lab and launched in 2016 to offer a more flexible, Python-friendly approach for building neural networks.

Background

Before PyTorch, Facebook researchers used Torch, a deep learning framework built in Lua. However, Lua’s limited popularity made integration with Python projects difficult, so Facebook sought a Python-based alternative.

Key Innovations

FAIR’s goal was to build a framework that balanced easy experimentation with strong production support. A major feature was dynamic computation graphs, allowing models to adjust on-the-fly rather than relying on pre-set graphs—making experimentation faster and more adaptable.

Influences and Community

Inspired by the Japanese framework Chainer, PyTorch adopted dynamic graphs and a Pythonic design, which quickly made it a favorite among researchers. Being open-source, PyTorch attracted a large community of contributors, helping it become a strong rival to TensorFlow.

Growth and Industry Adoption

After PyTorch 1.0’s 2018 release, which improved stability and production features, adoption surged in research and industry alike. Facebook and Microsoft’s partnership also extended PyTorch’s presence on cloud platforms, such as Azure.

Today

PyTorch has become a go-to for tasks across fields like computer vision and natural language processing, valued for its flexibility, simplicity, and strong community support.

We’ve all used classic UNIX command line utilities. For example, to count lines in a file:

> cat article.txt | wc -l
output: 46

Now, with Playbooks, you can create semantic, LLM-powered CLI utilities. For example:

> cat article.txt | summarize
output: The US penny, which cost nearly four cents to mint despite being worth one cent, was officially discontinued after 238 years of production. While the penny's removal from circulation is causing challenges for retailers and consumers - including rounding issues and potential legal complications in certain states - it will remain legal tender. The transition has been chaotic due to lack of government guidance, contrasting with how other countries like Canada and Australia handled similar currency phase-outs.

You can send a natural-language message to the utility to modify its behavior!

> cat article.txt | summarize --message "Use Pirate speak"
output: The penny, that scurvy dog of currency, has finally met Davy Jones' locker after 238 years o' sailin' the seven seas! The US Mint struck its final coin in June, and now merchants be facin' a tempest o' troubles—some be roundin' prices to the nearest nickel, while others be searchin' high and low fer pennies to keep their coffers balanced. Aye, 'tis a chaotic voyage ahead fer retailers and customers alike!

I use it to automate tasks like creating release notes by going through commit logs between two commits.
> release_notes --start v0.6.0 --end v0.7.0

This is same as
> playbooks run release_notes.pb --start v0.6.0 --end v0.7.0
output: See the release notes created with this utility at https://lnkd.in/gGjZrt8n

====

Here is another workflow: Search arXiv for today's papers on "AI agents", download the top 5 PDFs, convert each to markdown, extract future directions from each paper, then create a meta-summary as a bullet list of the most interesting research directions across all papers, and email the final synthesis to my@company.com with subject "Research proposals".

Do it in one line of bash script with semantic utilities search_arxiv and summarize --

search_arxiv --message "AI agents" | head -5 | xargs -I {}sh -c 'wget -qO- "{}" | pandoc -f pdf -t markdown | summarize --message "focus on future directions"'|\
summarize --message "Summarize as bullet list of most interesting research directions"|\
mail -s "Research proposals" my@company.com

post_text:
Cuándo tiene sentido la IA local: dispositivo, gateway o edge computer
"Edge AI" no describe un solo tipo de hardware. Elegir mal entre dispositivo IA dedicado, gateway edge o edge computer industrial es uno de los errores más caros en proyectos de analítica en tiempo real.
La decisión correcta depende de dos ejes independientes:
🔹 Intensidad de cómputo — ¿cuánto exige el workload?
🔹 Alcance de integración — ¿cuántos dispositivos, protocolos y funciones de red debe coordinar el hardware?
Dispositivo IA dedicado (ej. cámara con detección de objetos): ideal cuando una sola relación entrada-modelo-salida es estable. Fuerte en especialización, limitado en integración — no gestiona Modbus, múltiples PLCs ni backhaul celular.
Edge computing gateway: conecta equipos de campo, ejecuta aplicaciones locales y traslada datos seleccionados a sistemas superiores. Es la opción correcta cuando el resultado depende de combinar contexto — por ejemplo, vibración + corriente de motor + estado de PLC + entrada digital, para saber si una lectura elevada ocurrió en arranque o en producción normal.
Edge computer industrial: necesario solo cuando el proyecto exige varios streams de vídeo en alta resolución, modelos grandes, GPU o bases de datos pesadas — cargas que superan lo que una plataforma gateway-class puede ofrecer.
Un matiz importante: no todo gateway edge es un gateway de IA. El Robustel EG5100 es una plataforma sólida para bridging de protocolos y buffering, pero no incluye NPU dedicada. El EG5120 sí — añade CPU quad-core Cortex-A53 a 1.6GHz, hasta 4GB LPDDR4, 64GB eMMC y NPU de 2.3 TOPS, manteniendo routing celular, Ethernet Gigabit y gestión RCMS.
Y si el sitio necesita agregar más dispositivos (varias cámaras IP, más Ethernet, RS-422, HDMI, salidas de relé), el EG5200 ofrece la misma clase de CPU y NPU con 5 puertos Gigabit Ethernet frente a los 2 del EG5120 — la diferencia no es más potencia de IA, sino más alcance de integración.

post_text:
Task Runners in n8n: The Upgrade We've Been Waiting For 🚀

I've been experimenting with n8n's new Task Runners, and I have to say—it changes how you extend and scale workflows. Until recently, extending n8n Code nodes with custom dependencies meant rebuilding the entire n8n Docker image every time. This was heavyweight, slow to iterate, and forced you to mix untested libraries into your production container. Now, with Task Runners, it's finally clean and modular.

🧩 How it works
Task Runners move code execution from the main n8n process to separate workers — either as internal child processes or fully external containers. That means:
- Better isolation and stability
- Independent resource management (scale runners separately)
- Faster iteration when adding custom dependencies
- Improved security posture

🛠️ What's even better
Since Task Runners are bundled in the n8n Docker image but run as separate processes, you can:
- Build a custom Dockerfile extending the n8n image with your own JS/TS or Python dependencies
- Run it as an external task runner attached to your existing n8n instance
- Keep your main n8n container clean while extending capabilities for advanced workloads

And if you're running n8n at scale: Task Runners work seamlessly with Queue Mode, where n8n distributes workflow execution across multiple workers — each worker gets its own task runner for true horizontal scalability.

If you're running n8n with custom code requirements, Task Runners are worth exploring.

(不然我也是重度Netflix使用者啊，Netflix創辦人怎麼沒來找我拍影集)
實際攤開他的GitHub網站，高中就用JavaScript開發出網頁版Minecraft獲得關注，同時陸續複製各種遊戲，例如小精靈、神燈精靈，更開發模仿 Notion 和 Trello 的生產力工具，以及受typehere.co啟發打造的筆記工具 typehere.app。琳瑯滿目的專案，正是黃紹儒醉心於「building」的證明。

█用GitHub星星數當交換條件的家庭
黃紹儒從零開始打造產品的熱情，其實早就寫在他的 DNA 裡。
其父親、台大電機系教授黃鐘揚 Chung-Yang (Ric) Huang 曾加入矽谷新創，成為教授、組建家庭後也沒有放棄創業夢，創立了優拓資訊，黃鐘揚曾在受訪時表示：「骨子裡還是想要做出自己的產品。」黃紹儒從小耳濡目染，繼承爸爸的創業家精神，而且堅持要做自己有興趣的題目。
黃紹儒分享，爸爸曾要求自己做機器人專案，興致缺缺的他不願意聽從，只好條件交換：「爸爸說只要在GitHub拿到500顆星星，就不用做機器人。」為此黃紹儒更努力學習程式、開發產品，最後成功達到里程碑，換取父母不再干涉選題。
(其他家長是看成績單判斷小孩能力，黃家則是看GitHub星星數，這根本是工程師版「考到XX分就可以….」句型)

█新一代超能力
暫時放下學業，專注打造自己感興趣的產品的想法，已在黃紹儒心中萌芽許久。早在大二暑假，他就和黃鐘揚表達過想休學的念頭；為了能和Cursor團隊一起開發有趣的產品，即使要離鄉背井、休學也在所不惜。
尤其新創工作雖有趣也伴隨著壓力，黃紹儒在異鄉要面對隨時都可能被裁員的風險，他表示自己要學習爸爸在創業、家庭、工作三頭燒的狀況下還能「像一個石頭」一樣的定性，家庭給他的深刻影響與力量不言而喻。
除此之外，他做這一切的膽量與決心來自哪裡？當我在節目聽到黃紹儒分享自己最愛的影集是兩部經典的反英雄影集 — — 《黑袍糾察隊》和《無敵少俠》時，我猜想，也許下一個世代的超級英雄，就是要透過顛覆現狀，才能找到自我。

就像這兩部影集的主角，都曾崇拜英雄體制，但最終選擇走出自己的路。
而黃紹儒的選擇，其實也有一點這樣的影子。他沒有照著「念好書、進大公司」的安全劇本走，而是選擇休學、跳上目的未知AI列車，和世界級工程師肩並肩打造未來。

如今黃紹儒已經在GitHub上獲得超過2800顆星，是全台灣前十名的開發者，已經超過高中時爸爸給他的目標數5倍以上，現實世界裡他或許不會飛天或變身，但他與團隊用一行行程式碼，讓全世界已經超過五百萬名使用者能夠用AI賦能夢想，跨出夢想的第一步，這樣的力量，難道不就是新一代的超能力嗎？

author: Miguel Alho
post_text:
❓ Are you using local build tools or task runners like Cake Build, Nuke (for C#), Gulp, Grunt (JS) or any other that has the same utility for whatever stack you work in? If not, why?

I've noticed a trend over time, though some of the places I've worked over the past several years - there seems to be a drop in usage of them, and I can't necessarily put my finger on "why". Time ago, they were essential for productivity (and sanity), but that just doesn't seem to be the case anymore. There are a few things that come to mind though:

* As we've moved towards declarative builds in YAML files, there is less need to have an executable, procedural build script or task list to execute the build. In this case, the build vendor has some build model you can declare, and therefore you don't want to duplicate the effort of writing the build yourself, regardless of the possible lock-in.
* The microservice approach - small services in individual repos - may have the following effect: (1) too many repos, so setting up the build / task collection becomes overhead in each repo; (2) repos are simpler, so builds are simpler, so "something" simpler (a single script) is enough;
* Setup cost for the task colleciton is greater than copying scripts or commands, or some better way of sharing reusable bits were found, so the task manager had less benefit;
* Build definition, for whatever reason, has been offloaded to a seperate team, meaning that the tasks that would have been defined by these tools, would need to match that teams skills rather then the dev's knowledge set.

🤖 Van Software Testing naar AI Testing

AI-toepassingen worden steeds meer onderdeel van het softwarelandschap. Daarmee verandert ook de rol van Quality Assurance.

Bij traditionele softwaretests kunnen we voor een bepaalde input vaak een verwachte output definiëren. Bij systemen die gebaseerd zijn op LLM’s ligt dat anders: dezelfde input hoeft niet altijd exact dezelfde output op te leveren.

Daarom is alleen de vraag “Werkt het?” niet meer voldoende.

Bij het testen van AI-systemen moeten we ook kijken naar aspecten zoals factuality, relevance, hallucination, consistency, safety en response quality.

Om mijn kennis op dit gebied verder te ontwikkelen, heb ik de training LLM Evaluation (AI Testing) succesvol afgerond. 🎓

Tijdens de training heb ik mij onder andere verdiept in Promptfoo, Hugging Face, LLM-as-a-Judge, deterministic & non-deterministic evaluation, Red Team Testing en Model Auditing. LLM-Evaluation-Testing.pdf

Een belangrijk inzicht dat ik hieruit meeneem:

AI testen gaat niet alleen om controleren of een antwoord correct is. Het gaat ook om systematisch beoordelen hoe betrouwbaar, consistent, veilig en relevant een AI-systeem zich gedraagt.

Met mijn achtergrond in QA en Test Automation blijf ik mij verder ontwikkelen richting LLM Evaluation en AI Testing. 🚀

7 RAG Design Patterns You Must Know in 2026.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) isn't single architecture in 2026 it will be an ecosystem of specialized patterns designed for different business needs.

Here's a quick breakdown of the 7 RAG design patterns every AI builder should know:

🔹 Naive RAG
The foundation. Retrieve relevant chunks → send to LLM → generate response. Simple, fast, but often struggles with retrieval quality.

🔹 Retrieve-and-Rerank RAG
Adds a reranking layer to improve context relevance before generation. Higher accuracy, better answers.

🔹 Multimodal RAG
Retrieves from text, images, audio, and video. Essential for enterprise knowledge bases, healthcare, retail, and media applications.

🔹 GraphRAG
Uses knowledge graphs to capture relationships between entities. Powerful for complex reasoning and connected data exploration.

🔹 Hybrid RAG
Combines vector search + graph databases. Delivers both semantic understanding and structured relationship reasoning.

🔹 Agentic RAG (Router)
An AI agent decides which data source, retrieval strategy, or tool to use. Smarter orchestration, lower hallucination risk.

🔹 Multi-Agent RAG
Multiple specialized agents collaborate on retrieval, web search, tool usage, and synthesis. Best suited for advanced enterprise AI systems.

The teams that understand these patterns today will build the most reliable AI products tomorrow.

Top 25 Backend Concepts
(every serious software engineer should understand)

SYSTEM DESIGN
1. Load Balancing
↳ Distributes traffic across multiple servers.

2. Caching
↳ Stores frequently accessed data closer to the application.

3. Database Indexing
↳ Makes queries faster without scanning the entire dataset.

4. Replication
↳ Keeps copies of data across multiple nodes for availability.

5. Sharding
↳ Splits data across multiple databases when one can no longer handle the load.

DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS

6. Eventual Consistency
↳ Allows different nodes to temporarily have different versions of data.

7. Idempotency
↳ Ensures repeating a request doesn't create unintended duplicate effects.

8. Distributed Locks
↳ Prevents multiple workers from modifying the same resource simultaneously.

9. Leader Election
↳ Allows distributed nodes to agree on which node coordinates a task.

10. Consensus
↳ Helps distributed systems agree on shared state despite failures.

PERFORMANCE and RELIABILITY

11. Backpressure
↳ Prevents fast producers from overwhelming slower consumers.

12. Rate Limiting
↳ Controls how many requests a client can make within a given period.

13. Circuit Breakers
↳ Stops repeatedly calling a failing dependency.

14. Retries
↳ Reattempts failed operations when failures are likely temporary.

15. Timeouts
↳ Prevents your system from waiting indefinitely for a dependency.

ASYNCHRONOUS SYSTEMS
16. Message Queues
↳ Decouple producers from consumers and process work asynchronously.

17. Pub/Sub
↳ Allows multiple consumers to react to the same event.

18. Dead Letter Queues
↳ Stores messages that repeatedly fail processing.

19. Consumer Groups
↳ Distributes messages across consumers for parallel processing.

20. At-Least-Once Delivery
↳ Requires you to design for duplicate messages and safe retries.

DATA and ARCHITECTURE

21. Transactions
↳ Keeps related database operations consistent.

22. Connection Pooling
↳ Reuses database connections instead of creating one per request.

23. CQRS
↳ Separates read and write models when their requirements differ.

24. Observability
↳ Uses logs, metrics, and traces to understand system behavior.

25. Disaster Recovery
↳ Defines how systems recover when infrastructure or data fails.

Don’t just memorize them.
Understand how they work together.

Over the past few weeks, I wanted to understand Model Context Protocol (MCP) beyond basic implementations, so I built a real-world system where an AI agent can investigate failing data pipelines using operational data.

🔎 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗮: When a data pipeline fails, can an AI agent systematically investigate the incident instead of simply generating a guess?🧠
How it works:
A user can ask:
“Investigate the customer_sync pipeline and determine why it is failing.”

The LLM dynamically decides which information it needs and uses MCP tools to investigate:
• Pipeline status
• Recent pipeline runs
• Pipeline logs
• Pipeline dependencies
• Incident timelines
• Recent deployments
• Database health
The retrieved information is converted into structured evidence, maintained throughout the investigation, and used to generate a final report containing:
Summary → Severity → Confidence → Evidence → Hypotheses → Recommendations → Uncertainty

🔌 𝗔 𝗸𝗲𝘆 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁 : I built both the MCP Client and MCP Server rather than only consuming an existing MCP server.

Working on both sides gave me a much deeper understanding of the complete MCP system , from tool discovery and invocation to tool exposure, request handling, and integration with application services and PostgreSQL.
🔍 Example
In one investigation, the agent collected evidence showing:
crm-service deployment
↓
email column returned JSONB
↓
transformation expected VARCHAR
↓
schema mismatch
↓
customer_sync failed

The final report separates evidence, hypotheses, and uncertainty rather than presenting assumptions as facts.
🏗️ 𝗔𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲
LLM → MCP Client → MCP Server → Investigation Tools → Services → PostgreSQL → Evidence → Final Report🛠️
𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗰𝗸: Python | MCP | Groq | PostgreSQL | SQLAlchemy | Docker | uv

author: Jim Jansen
post_text:
Assessing inter-rater agreement among large language model judges: Evidence from persona evaluation across varying educational risk contexts

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as automated judges for evaluation, yet their reliability remains unclear.

In this research, led by Danial Amin, this study examines the inter-rater agreement of three LLM judges (GPT-4o, Claude 3 Sonnet, and Gemini 1.5 Pro) when evaluating fairness, lack of stereotypicality, and diversity in user personas across varying educational risk contexts.

We analyzed 60 individual personas and 12 persona sets to assess whether these judges demonstrate sufficient consistency to function as reliable evaluators.

Although inter-rater agreement was moderate at the individual persona level, three critical limitations emerged.

At the set level, agreement ranged from .39 to .63 across persona generators and therefore did not show a uniform decline relative to individual-level agreement. Mean dimension-support scores were 41% to 61% lower, although the individual- and set-level tasks are not directly comparable.

Second, non-compliance rates, where judges could not provide textual justification for their ratings, ranged from 9.6 to 26.7% at the individual level and increased to 34% to 49% at the set level.

Third, agreement differed across the three educational scenarios classified by risk: individual-level agreement declined from the lower- to higher-risk scenarios, while set-level agreement showed no monotonic pattern. We conclude that, under the tested protocol, current LLM judges demonstrate poor-to-moderate inter-rater agreement for persona evaluation.

These findings provide a descriptive characterization of LLM evaluation behavior across risk contexts and lay the foundation for future validation studies comparing LLM agreement with human judgment.

Amin, D., Salminen, J., and Jansen, B. J. (2027) Assessing Inter-Rater Agreement Among Large Language Model Judges: Evidence from Persona Evaluation Across Varying Educational Risk Contexts, Technological Forecasting amp; Social Change. Article: 124894,

author: Roberto Heckers
post_text:
Did you know ng new, even in strict mode, leaves one of the most useful #TypeScript flags off? 👀

noUncheckedIndexedAccess. One line in tsconfig.json.

Without it, TypeScript tells you orders[0] is an Order. It is not. It is an Order, or undefined when the array is empty. Same for a Record lookup with a key nobody ever set. The type lies, the code reads fine, and the production error says "Cannot read properties of undefined".

With the flag on, every index read becomes T | undefined. You add a ?. or an early return, and that bug can no longer compile ✅

The flag reaches further than most people expect: it applies inside your #Angular templates too. The template type checker generates plain TypeScript from your template, so it inherits every compiler option. orders()[0].id in an interpolation or o.lines[0].sku inside an @for block fails the build with TS2532, the same error you would get in the class.

Angular's extended diagnostics account for it as well. With the flag off, the compiler deliberately stays quiet about a fallback on an indexed read like items[0], because it knows the non-nullable type cannot be trusted there. With it on, the type is honest and the diagnostics can be too.

Turning it on in an existing codebase costs an afternoon. Most fixes are a question mark. A few are real bugs you did not know you had, and those pay for the afternoon.

MCP Architecture — The Missing Layer Between AI and Real-World Systems

AI models are powerful.

But an LLM alone cannot directly understand your databases, APIs, files, cloud services, internal tools, or enterprise systems.

That’s where Model Context Protocol (MCP) comes in.

MCP provides a standardized way for AI applications to connect with external tools and data.

The basic architecture:

AI Application / MCP Client
↓
MCP Protocol — JSON-RPC 2.0
↓
MCP Server
↓
Tools + Resources + Prompts
↓
Databases | APIs | Files | Cloud | SaaS | Custom Systems

A typical flow looks like:

1. Client sends a request
2. MCP server receives the request
3. Server invokes the required tool or resource
4. External system processes the request
5. Structured result is returned
6. LLM uses the result to generate the final response

For AI Test Engineers, MCP introduces an entirely new testing surface:

• Tool invocation validation
• JSON-RPC request/response validation
• Schema validation
• Authentication & authorization testing
• Prompt injection testing
• Tool poisoning testing
• Access-control testing
• Error handling & timeout testing
• Data leakage testing
• MCP server reliability testing

MCP is not just an AI integration concept.

It is becoming an important architecture layer for building and testing AI-powered systems.

Save this architecture for your MCP + AI Testing journey.

¿Crees que un contenedor comprometido no puede tocar tu servidor? 🐳
Una nueva vulnerabilidad de Docker, CVE-2026-17106 (CopyEscape), pone el foco en una frontera que muchas veces damos por aislada:
contenedor → host
La vulnerabilidad afecta a docker cp y puede permitir que archivos sean escritos fuera del directorio de destino esperado.
🔎 Revisé mi propio entorno y tenía Docker Engine 29.5.2, dentro del rango afectado.
Lo actualicé a 29.8.2 y quedó corregido.
Si usas Docker, revisa primero:
docker version
Y actualiza Docker Engine desde el repositorio oficial de tu distribución:
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade
o, según tu distribución:
sudo dnf upgrade docker-ce
Después, vuelve a comprobar:
docker version
⚠️ No revises solamente tus imágenes. El Docker Engine, runners de CI/CD y operaciones que cruzan hacia el host también forman parte de la superficie de ataque.
Si utilizas docker cp en pipelines o automatizaciones, vale la pena revisarlo.
